rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, all design choices are uncertain. The most informative first experiment is a standard, moderate multimodal baseline that anchors the design space for all future comparisons. config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) uses well-understood, standard components at each dimension: PCA for RNA (simple, fast, no training), ResNet-50 for image (standard pretrained backbone), avgpool for aggregation (simple, interpretable), and concat for fusion (simple, no learned weights). This places it near the center of the configuration space, so every subsequent experiment—varying RNA encoder (scvi/scgpt), image encoder (ViT-L), aggregation (transformer), fusion (weighted), profile setting (singleprofile), or modality (rna_only/image_only)—constitutes a clean single-variable comparison against this baseline. Starting with the simplest reasonable multimodal pipeline also lets us determine whether the basic architecture is functional before investing budget in more complex encoders or fusion strategies, maximizing the information gained per experiment under the limited budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_004: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat → 61.9% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality actually contributes meaningful signal over RNA alone. config_029 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_004: the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation are all identical; only the image modality is removed. If RNA alone achieves comparable accuracy, it would collapse the search space by eliminating the need to optimize image encoders, fusion strategies, and cross-modal aggregation—saving many experiments. If RNA alone is substantially worse, it confirms multimodal fusion is essential and justifies investing subsequent experiments in encoder and fusion choices. Establishing this modality-level baseline before exploring encoder variants (scvi, scgpt, ViT-L) or fusion strategies (weighted, transformer) is the highest-information use of the next budget slot.

We have a multimodal baseline (config_004: pca_n2000+resnet50+avgpool+concat, acc=0.619) and an RNA-only baseline (config_029: pca_n2000+avgpool, acc=0.591), showing a ~2.8% accuracy gain from adding image. However, we lack an image-only baseline to decompose the contribution of each modality. config_039 (image_only, multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool) is the cleanest complement: it shares the same image encoder (resnet50), profile setting (multiprofile), and aggregation (avgpool) as the two completed experiments. This lets us isolate whether the image modality contributes independently or whether the multimodal gain is synergistic. Understanding this is critical before investing further experiments in more complex multimodal variants (different encoders, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion), as it tells us whether the image signal is a meaningful additive component or a minor correction. Under a limited budget, completing the modality decomposition (RNA-only, image-only, multimodal) with matched hyperparameters is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: config_004 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.6186 acc, while config_029 (RNA-only, same pca_n2000) achieves 0.5907 and config_039 (image-only, resnet50) only 0.3275. RNA is clearly the dominant signal, and the multimodal gain over RNA-alone is modest (+2.8%). This suggests the RNA representation may be the bottleneck. Question: Does replacing the simple PCA encoder (pca_n2000) with a learned variational autoencoder (scvi_n200) improve performance in the multimodal setting? config_007 changes only the RNA encoder relative to config_004, keeping image encoder (resnet50), aggregation (avgpool), fusion (concat), and profile setting (multiprofile) identical. This clean single-variable comparison isolates the effect of RNA representation quality. Why best next experiment: Since RNA drives most of the signal, improving its encoder is the highest-leverage design decision. A positive result would justify further investment in more complex RNA encoders (e.g., scgpt); a null result would indicate PCA is sufficient and redirect attention to fusion or image-encoder choices. Under a limited budget, this experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful design axis.

Evidence: config_007 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat, multiprofile) is the current best at 0.6315 acc, and RNA is the dominant modality (0.5907) while image is weak (0.3275), suggesting asymmetric modality importance. Uncertainty: we have only tested concat fusion; it is unclear whether weighted fusion—letting the model learn per-modality importance—would better exploit this asymmetry or whether the simple concatenation is already sufficient. This experiment (config_005) changes only the fusion strategy from concat to weighted while holding the best-known settings (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, multiprofile) constant, giving a clean single-variable comparison against config_007. It is the best use of the next budget slot because fusion is the core mechanism for combining modalities, the result will inform all future multimodal configurations, and a single-variable design avoids confounding with other untested dimensions (image encoder, aggregation, profile setting).

Evidence: config_005 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the best at 0.6776 acc, and we've established scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 and weighted > concat. However, the image modality alone is very weak (0.3275 with resnet50), so it's unclear whether the image contribution is bottlenecked by encoder capacity. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l improve the multimodal model while holding the best-known RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (avgpool), and fusion (weighted) fixed? This is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005. Why this is the best next experiment: it directly extends the current best configuration along the highest-uncertainty axis (image representation quality), and the result will tell us whether further investment in image-side design is worthwhile or whether the RNA signal dominates regardless of image encoder strength.

The current best config (config_021: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.7062 acc. We have strong evidence that weighted fusion and ViT-L image encoder are beneficial, but aggregation has only been tested as avgpool. With multiprofile, multiple cell profiles must be combined, and a transformer aggregation could capture inter-profile interactions that simple mean pooling discards. Config_049 changes only aggregation (avgpool→transformer) relative to config_021, cleanly isolating the effect of the aggregation mechanism while holding all other design choices at their empirically validated best values. This is the most informative exploitation step: if transformer aggregation improves performance, it identifies a new productive design axis; if not, it confirms avgpool sufficiency and redirects budget toward other unexplored dimensions (e.g., scgpt encoder or singleprofile).

Evidence: The current best (config_049: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc=0.725) shows consistent gains from each design upgrade (scvi>pca, ViT>ResNet, weighted>concat, transformer>avgpool). However, the fusion effect was only validated with avgpool aggregation (config_005 vs config_007: +0.046). With transformer aggregation, the learned attention mechanism may already capture modality-level weighting, potentially making explicit weighted fusion redundant. Question: Does weighted fusion still provide a meaningful advantage over simple concat when paired with transformer aggregation? config_009 is identical to config_049 except fusion=concat, giving a clean single-variable A/B test. Why best next: It directly clarifies whether one of our key design choices (weighted fusion) is truly necessary or subsumed by the transformer, which affects both final architecture complexity and whether further fusion-level exploration is warranted. Under a limited budget, isolating this interaction at the top-performing configuration is more informative than jumping to an untested RNA encoder (scgpt) that would confound multiple variables.

The current best (config_049: scvi_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.7250, and we have strong evidence that image encoder (ViT-L > ResNet50), aggregation (transformer > avgpool), and weighted fusion all contribute to performance. However, the RNA encoder choice remains underexplored at the top of the performance range: we've only tested pca_n2000 and scvi_n200, with a small gap (~1.3%) between them. config_043 (scgpt, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_049, isolating the effect of the scgpt RNA encoder in the context of the strongest image pipeline. If scgpt outperforms scvi_n200, it identifies a new promising representation axis to exploit; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 as the optimal RNA encoder and redirects budget toward other axes (e.g., profile setting or fusion refinement). This is the most informative next step because the RNA encoder is a fundamental representation choice, the comparison is controlled (only one variable changes), and the outcome directly determines whether further RNA-encoder exploration is warranted under the limited budget.

Evidence: All 9 completed experiments are multiprofile multimodal or single-modality baselines. The best config (config_049, scvi_n200 + vit_l + transformer + weighted) reaches 0.725, but the incremental gain from switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in the multimodal setting was only +0.013 (config_004→config_007), which is small and could be confounded by the image signal. Meanwhile, the rna_only baseline with pca_n2000 (config_029) sits at 0.591. Question: config_015 (rna_only, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_029 (rna_only, pca_n2000, avgpool), isolating the RNA encoder effect without any image or fusion confounds. If scvi_n200 rna_only reaches ~0.68-0.70, the RNA encoder is the primary driver and further gains should target RNA representation; if it stays near 0.59, the image+aggregation pipeline is essential and we should prioritize image-side improvements. This is the highest-information experiment under budget because it decomposes the source of the 0.725 performance, directly guiding whether remaining experiments should focus on the RNA encoder, the image encoder/aggregation, or the profile setting.
